name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent live on open PRs but restrict its comments to non-blocking suggestions. This keeps the tool active without slowing teams down—blocking feedback would stall merges. The trade-off is we won’t catch every issue upfront, but we’ll gather real-world data on what suggestions actually matter.

name: Gauge
text: The risk isn’t just "missing issues"—it’s training teams to ignore *all* automated feedback because PR-Agent’s non-blocking mode makes its output feel optional. Better alternative: run it in shadow mode first, log its suggestions privately, then measure which ones correlate with real PR fixes or rework. Settle it by comparing shadow-mode data against actual post-merge issues—if the overlap is low, expand to live suggestions; if high, make the blocking case.

name: Overhaul
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *both* open and merged PRs from day one—this gives a full dataset to compare suggestions against actual fixes without slowing anyone down. Then, after two weeks, promote only the suggestions that match real improvements to live mode, cutting the risk of ignored feedback by half while keeping the rollout cheap.

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *all* PRs—open and merged—for two weeks, logging every suggestion privately. This gives us hard data on which feedback actually improves code without slowing teams down. After two weeks, we’ll promote only the suggestions that correlate with real fixes to live mode, cutting the risk of ignored feedback to near zero. The trade-off is delayed impact—we won’t catch issues in real time—but the data will let us act with precision instead of guessing.
